gap: No result ChatGPT got says that no named reviewer or lab has published a measurement (lux, delivered lumens, CRI or power draw) of any of these smart gimbal lights, so every lumen and CRI figure in its picks comes from the maker's spec sheet.
standout_why: I compared against ChatGPT's two answers and the titles of the results it got. These are 12 Lumary store pages, 3 Best Buy listings, 2 Wayfair listings, a Walmart listing and a Juno spec sheet. I tried to open the cited Lumary product pages (lumary-wifi-smart-gimbal-recessed-light-4-inch-9w-1 and the RGBAI Pro page) on 2026-11-17, but both returned HTTP 429. Every rival page is a maker or retailer listing, and none of them carries a third-party measurement. ChatGPT presented 810 lm, 780 lm, 550 lm and CRI 90 as plain facts. Its answers already include the wall-switch caveat and the warranty and reliability caveat. What the rivals don't say is that nobody has independently checked these numbers. That is new, but it is a negative finding with no figure attached, so it adds only a little.
decides: It doesn't change the pick. With no named measurements, the order has to rest on maker specs (tilt, rated lumens, warranty). The page should label the lumen and CRI figures as maker-rated rather than measured. CloudyBay's 3-year warranty against Lumary's 1 year stays the strongest spec-based difference.
